answer: Each submission hangs on the zenith of a task receipt, and the forge is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, diluted when peers disagree, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The horizon of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
